item.title: Entrepreneurial ethics: moral cognition, affect, and action under uncertainty
item.content:encoded:
This special issue explores the ethical dimensions of entrepreneurship, focusing on how entrepreneurs engage in moral reasoning and decision-making. The call seeks research that examines the cognitive and emotional processes underlying ethical choices that entrepreneurs face, particularly in contexts marked by uncertainty and risk. The issue aims to advance understanding of how moral considerations shape entrepreneurial behavior and venture development.

Researchers are invited to submit work investigating the intersection of ethics, cognition, and emotion in entrepreneurial contexts. The special issue welcomes diverse perspectives on how entrepreneurs navigate ethical dilemmas, the role of affect in moral judgments, and mechanisms through which ethical considerations translate into concrete actions during the venture creation process.

Appel publié par Journal of Business Venturing. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Moral cognition in entrepreneurship
  • Affective processes in ethical decision-making
  • Ethical action under uncertainty
  • Entrepreneurial decision-making and ethics
  • Moral reasoning in venture creation
  • Emotional dimensions of ethical behavior

Timeline

  • September 1, 2027: Submission deadline

item.title: Advancing Project Management through Data Science: Methods, Applications, and Impacts
item.content:encoded:
This special issue examines how data science reshapes project, programme, and portfolio management practices. Rather than focusing on technical algorithmic details, it seeks to understand how managers can translate data and algorithmic insights into better decisions, governance, and value creation across the project lifecycle. The collection emphasizes managerial transformation rather than technology as an add-on.

Contributions should address how data-driven practices improve decision quality and accountability, how governance mechanisms adapt to data-intensive work, and how manager and team competencies evolve. The special issue particularly welcomes research on adoption conditions, implementation challenges, and safeguards for ethical use, bias mitigation, and transparency in decision-making.

Submissions should prioritize actionable insights for practitioners through conceptual frameworks, empirical case studies, and practical artifacts such as decision frameworks, governance templates, and maturity models. Cross-sector studies demonstrating tangible managerial outcomes and connections to organizational strategy and broader societal value are especially encouraged.

Appel publié par International Journal of Managing Projects in Business. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Data-driven decision-making in project environments: Exploring how data science enhances or transforms decision processes across the project lifecycle, including planning, monitoring, and risk management emphasizing chances, challenges and risk.
  • Integration of data science methodologies into project management practices: Studies applying or adapting methods such as machine learning, data mining, or predictive analytics to project-specific contexts.
  • Data science and project governance, ethics, and accountability: Examining the implications of algorithmic decision-making, data privacy, and ethical use of data in managing projects.
  • The evolving role of the project manager in data-rich contexts: Investigating new competencies, skills, and leadership styles required for managing data-intensive or AI-augmented projects. Discussing the relationship between project managers and data science experts in project management.
  • Real-time data, dashboards and analytics for project monitoring and control: Contributions on the design and limits, use and evaluation of real-time performance tracking and visualisation tools in project management.
  • Data ecosystems and infrastructure in large-scale or complex projects: Studies addressing the architecture, integration, and governance of data sources across distributed project networks.
  • Cross-disciplinary applications of data science in projects: Interdisciplinary work linking project management with fields such as operations research, information systems, computational social science, or engineering.
  • AI, big data and automation in project scheduling, forecasting, and resource allocation: Empirical or conceptual work on how intelligent systems are used to optimize project efficiency and adaptability.
  • Data-enabled project evaluation, benefits realisation, and impact assessment: Using data science to better measure and predict the value, outcomes, and sustainability of projects, including alignment with SDGs.
  • Theoretical and conceptual contributions linking data science and project studies: Frameworks and models that critically examine the intersection of data science and project management as evolving disciplines.
  • AI-empowered stakeholder engagement in large-scale or complex projects: Leveraging AI to enhance stakeholder analysis, communication, and collaboration in complex projects, optimizing engagement strategies and improving project outcomes through predictive insights and automated interaction tools.

Timeline

  • January 4, 2026: Opening date for manuscripts submissions
  • July 31, 2026: Closing date for abstract submission
  • January 31, 2027: Closing date for manuscripts submission

item.title: Exploring the Interplay of Entrepreneurial Emotion, Judgment, and Decision Making
item.content:encoded:
This special issue examines how emotions influence entrepreneurial judgment and decision-making, particularly in community-based and localized ecosystems. While existing research has focused on positive emotions like passion and resilience, the issue seeks to explore understudied emotional domains such as despair, awe, humility, guilt, empathy, and regret that shape entrepreneurs' strategic choices, resilience, and ethical judgments.

The special issue welcomes interdisciplinary research on how diverse emotional experiences affect entrepreneurial cognition and behavior within small businesses, family firms, and social enterprises. It invites both quantitative approaches examining causal relationships and qualitative studies exploring contextualized experiences, alongside theoretical contributions offering new frameworks for understanding emotions in entrepreneurship.

Insights from this research aim to inform policy-making, entrepreneurial education, and support structures by revealing how emotional dynamics drive sustainable business practices, ethical decision-making, and community engagement in localized entrepreneurial ecosystems.

item.title: Game Theoretical Models and Applications SING21

This special issue focuses on game theory as a framework for studying strategic behavior, cooperation, and decision-making in complex systems. It welcomes research on both theoretical developments and practical applications across diverse fields, with emphasis on interaction dynamics and collective decision-making.

The issue particularly encourages submissions from participants of the European Meeting on Game Theory 2026 (SING21), who are invited to submit expanded versions of their conference papers. Other submissions in game theory and related applications are also welcome.

item.title: Multiple Objective Programming and Goal Programming: Artificial Intelligence for Decision Making in Economic and Social Sciences
item.content:encoded:
Matteo Rocca, University of Insubria

Davide La Torre, Skema Business School

Constantin Zopounidis, Technical University of Crete

This special issue seeks papers that integrate multiple objective programming, goal programming, and artificial intelligence to address complex decision-making in economic and social sciences. The issue welcomes both substantially extended papers from the 16th International Conference on Multiple Objective Programming and Goal Programming (MOPGP'25) held in Varese, Italy, and original work not previously presented at the conference.

Multiple objective optimization and goal programming provide structured frameworks for evaluating conflicting objectives, while artificial intelligence enhances these approaches through data analytics and machine learning. The combination enables processing of large datasets and improves the accuracy and robustness of decision models and predictions in addressing real-world challenges.

item.title: The evolution of decision-making and reasoning from childhood to adulthood
item.content:encoded:
,

,

This special issue examines how decision-making processes, choice behavior, and reasoning capabilities evolve from childhood through adulthood. Understanding the developmental trajectory of these fundamental cognitive and behavioral processes provides insight into the mechanisms that underlie human judgment and decision-making across the lifespan.

The collection seeks to integrate perspectives from developmental psychology, behavioral economics, cognitive science, and neuroscience to explore how individuals acquire, refine, and modify their decision-making strategies as they mature. Contributions may address the biological, cognitive, social, and environmental factors that shape the development of choice behavior and reasoning abilities.

Empirical studies, theoretical frameworks, and methodological approaches that advance our understanding of developmental decision-making are welcome. This includes research examining both normative development and individual variation in how people learn to make choices and engage in reasoning from early childhood through adulthood.

Appel publié par Journal of Behavioral and Experimental Economics. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • The role of emotions and affect in developing choice behavior
  • Neural and biological substrates of reasoning development
  • Individual differences in decision-making trajectories
  • The impact of education and experience on choice behavior
  • Temporal and risk preferences across development
  • Social influences on reasoning and decision-making
  • Irrational choice patterns and their developmental origins

item.title: The Power of Difference: Strategic Decision-Making in Identity-Diverse Teams
item.content:encoded:
This special issue explores how identity diversity influences strategic decision-making processes within teams. We seek to understand the mechanisms through which diverse team compositions affect decision quality, creativity, and organizational outcomes. The focus is on examining both the benefits and challenges of managing identity-diverse teams in contemporary organizational settings.

item.title: AI-Driven Decision Making under Uncertain Environments: Theory, Methods, and Industrial Applications
item.content:encoded:

Jang Ho Kim, Korea University

This special issue addresses decision-making in complex industrial systems facing dynamic uncertainty through artificial intelligence and optimization techniques. The issue seeks research combining AI methods such as reinforcement learning, generative AI, and digital twins with operations research and optimization approaches to manage manufacturing, supply chains, healthcare, and other sectors dealing with demand fluctuations and disruptions.

The special issue welcomes both theoretical and practical contributions demonstrating how AI-driven methodologies can improve decision-making under uncertainty. Particular emphasis is placed on interdisciplinary research with clear industrial applicability and the adoption of open science practices including data and code sharing to enhance reproducibility.

item.title: From Individuals to Organizations: Unpacking Behavioral Issues in Supply Chain Risk Management
item.content:encoded:
Jon F. Kirchoff, East Carolina University

Ying Liao, East Carolina University

Shingirai Chris Kwaramba, Virginia Commonwealth University

Supply chain risk management traditionally assumes decision-makers are rational and risk-neutral, but practitioners operate under bounded rationality and cognitive biases, deviating from optimal choices when facing uncertainty. These behavioral deviations affect risk identification, assessment, and mitigation, yet existing theories fail to account for them, resulting in suboptimal strategies and reduced organizational efficiency.

Current behavioral SCRM research focuses primarily on individual factors with limited exploration of how organizational and inter-organizational contexts shape behavior. This special issue examines behavioral issues across multiple analytical levels: individuals, organizations, and supply chain networks. The editors seek research that identifies limitations in existing theories or introduces innovative frameworks addressing SCRM complexities through interdisciplinary perspectives from psychology, organizational studies, and decision-making research.

Appel publié par International Journal of Physical Distribution & Logistics Management. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.
